announcements.text: SupplyCore Inc.,* Rockford, Illinois, has been awarded a maximum $90,000,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for facilities maintenance, repair and operations supplies. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a 396-day bridge contract with no option periods. announcements.text: NAG LLC, Virginia Beach, Virginia, is awarded a $39,441,631 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the procurement of shipboard Radar Tank Level Indicator computer hardware. Under this contract, NAG LLC will provide materials required for the design, development, fabrication, testing, repair, and fleet implementation of TLI systems. Work will be performed in Virginia Beach, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 1, 2031. Fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,152,562 will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the System for Award Management website, with one responsible offer received. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N64498-26-D-1001).

announcements.text: Integer Technologies LLC,* Columbia, South Carolina, is awarded a $10,220,910 modification (CLIN 0002) to contract (N0001426C1129) for research and development for cyber-physical systems in Navy infrastructure. This contract provides for the exercise of Option One. The Louisiana State University and Integer Technologies partnership is advancing a cyber-physical resilience framework designed to safeguard the Navy’s maritime platforms. This proposal for Navy Embedded Systems outlines a structured, phased approach that begins with a comprehensive assessment of emerging cyber-physical vulnerabilities and culminates in the operational deployment of defense solutions across naval vessels and shore facilities. By integrating advanced simulation models, real-time dashboards and edge-hardening techniques, the program aims to deliver actionable insights that enhance mission effectiveness and protect critical systems from sophisticated adversaries. Work will be performed in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and is expected to be completed in March 2030. The amount of this action is $10,220,910, increasing the total cumulative contract value to $10,468,515. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $10,220,910 are obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Office of Naval Research, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Sierra Nevada Corp., Englewood, Colorado, has been awarded a $31,789,335 cost-reimbursement-fixed-fee, cost-reimbursement-no-fee, and firm-fixed-price contract for non-recurring engineering. This contract provides for design, development, and analysis of a post-production modification kit to convert a standard production XC-130J aircraft into a ski-equipped LC-130J. Work will be performed at Colorado Springs, Colorado, and is expected to be completed March 27, 2028. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2025 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $31,789,335 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Warner Robins, Georgia, is the contracting activity (FA8509-26-C-B001). (Awarded Sept. 1, 2026).

announcements.text: Aptima Inc., Woburn, Massachusetts, (FA2384-26-D-B004); and BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems Inc., Broomfield, Colorado (FA2384-26-D-B009), were awarded a ceiling $26,200,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for holistic models for decision-making. This contract provides for research to develop computational and mathematical models that simulate the effects of operational environment on warfighter performance. Work will be performed in Woburn, Massachusetts; Broomfield, Colorado; and Dayton, Ohio; and is expected to be completed by Aug. 24, 2034. These contracts were competitive acquisitions, and nine offers were received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $9,836 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 1, 2026).
